posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Got pretty lucky with the randomized start--Wager Master didn't play any of his nasty cards. First two (besides pretty benign opening conditions) cards played were Breaking the Rules, and then it was A Burning Sense of Failure. So no big threat, really.

Breaking the Rules was out the whole game, which always makes things interesting. Like having Impale and Turret Bot go off on the turn you play them. Frustrating for most of Unity's bots, though. You have to be patient for them to start to work.

Setback ended up doing the most through random Risk-y card plays in an already highly random game...High Risk Behavior had him dishing out big damage.

Saw Frazzat, Phrentat and Szreem. Bloogo came out at the end, but didn't do anything. Setback finished Wager Master off with a Karmic Retribution.

 

Setback 4 HP, Absolute Zero 6 HP, Unity and Expatriette both at 12HP and Scholar at 22HP.

posts.cooked:
I started with Who Are You Fighting?. My MO was to keep him on his front side until he was close enough to be defeated in one round after flipping. This meant keeping three Wagelings in play for 3 damage to all hero targets per round, and Venox was played early as well for 2 more damage per round, so it was a little dangerous to the heroes, but we managed to get setup for a fast victory upon flipping.

I didn't want to flip him right away because I didn't want him to have multiple opportunities at flipping WAYF? back. With my game, he had only a 1-in-5 chance of flipping WAYF?, and instead he flipped a Wagelings.

posts.name: seesome
posts.cooked:
Mint, but one of the most brutal Wager Master fights I've ever had.

 

WM got out both copies of What Do You Really Know early. I've seen this card before and it never bugged me much, but two at one is really nasty, especially since they don't flip, but are still indestructible. With both out, WM was acting as a super-Ambuscade, filling his deck with 8 bombs a turn, each of which does 4hp damage and then reveals the next card.  Luckily, he never got any other particularly nasty cards out so it just turned into a damage race, which I was just barely able to beat him at.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked: Full mint.  Last time I posted, I was stymied by a loop while I was within reach of victory.  It turned out to be an interaction between "Not All He Seems" and "A Burning Sense of Failure".  "Not All He Seems" is indestructible, but "A Burning Sense of Failure" is not.  Unfortunately, Unity didn't have a Bee Bot, Expatriette couldn't find her RPG Launcher, and Scholar has no Ongoing destruction at all.  Setback had Whoops, Sorry, but his turn had already passed.  Fortunately, AZ was able to save me with Fueled Freeze, and then Setback used Wrong Time and Place to redirect Venox's damage from the heroes to Wager Master, finishing him off with unlucky tokens to spare.

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
Mint. Got Playing Dice, Wageling, Losing to the Odds, Wageling. Then Who are you Fighting, but I won the next round by putting everyone at odd health, throat jabbing WM himself, and getting lucky with an environment play. He played Breaking the Rules, the Wageling made our healths even, and we won.

It seemed a lot longer to me than it was, because I agonized over whether to set our health to even and hope the environment hit us for an odd amount, or Immutus came out, or hope for the best and go odd. Then I got tired (Narcolepsy FTL), took a nap, and came back to it the next day.

We ended up with the fish (can’t remember his name) who hit a Wageling. We were safe.

I got Who Are You Fighting and a handful of Wagelings to start.
That was too many villain targets for comfort so I took out 2 Wagelings to flip the Master right away. Unfortunately he flipped Who Are You Fighting first off so I had to wade through 5 rounds whittling him down in HP while hoping another Wageling doesn’t get played. It worked out though, I flipped him, flipped him back (Wageling up this time,) and took him down for the Mint.

The Endlings didn’t really do much so except for using Whoops to take out the Refuge I let them be.

Expat starting with Speed Loading and Hollowpoints was pretty helpful I must say, especially when Scholar played a Shotgun off the top of her deck.
